fact_text: The Civic has been one of the best-selling compact cars in the US since it launched in 1972.
The original Mustang was designed to be affordable, sporty, and customizable — a formula that created the 'pony car' category.
The Corolla is the best-selling car nameplate in automotive history, with over 50 million sold worldwide.
The 1969 Camaro is one of the most recognizable muscle cars, known for its aggressive styling and big-block V8 options.
The original Beetle's rear-mounted, air-cooled engine design stayed remarkably consistent for over 65 years of production.
The Wrangler's boxy silhouette and round headlights trace their design lineage directly back to WWII military Jeeps.
The Accord was one of the first Japanese cars to be manufactured in the United States, starting in Marysville, Ohio in 1982.
The Camry has been the best-selling car in America for the majority of years since 1997.
The F-Series has been the best-selling vehicle (not just truck) in the US for decades running.
The original Miata (MX-5) was inspired by classic British roadsters but built with Japanese reliability, and holds the Guinness World Record for best-selling two-seat convertible.
